sentences.text: Great leaders are sometimes praised for their drive and sometimes for their teamwork.
Some people argue that successful leaders must be highly competitive, while others claim they must be willing to cooperate with others.
I believe both qualities matter, though I lean toward the view that cooperation is the more important of the two.
First, a degree of competitiveness genuinely helps leaders succeed.
A strong drive to win pushes leaders to set high goals and work tirelessly to reach them.
For example, a competitive business leader may fight hard to make her company the best in its field.
This shows that a competitive spirit can fuel ambition, energy, and real achievement.
Leaders without any drive to succeed may settle for far too little.
Competition can also push a whole team to perform at its very best.
To this extent, competitiveness is a useful quality in a leader.
Second, however, the ability to cooperate is at least as important, and often more so.
No leader achieves much alone, since real success depends on the work of many people.
Consider a leader who unites a divided team and inspires everyone to pull in the same direction.
Such cooperation can accomplish far more than any single competitive individual ever could.
A purely competitive leader may make enemies and destroy the trust that teams depend on.
Cooperation builds the loyalty and goodwill that hold an organisation together over time.
For these reasons, I find cooperation the more vital quality of the two.
In conclusion, successful leaders do benefit from a healthy competitive drive.
But the ability to cooperate matters even more, since no leader succeeds alone.
The best leaders combine the drive to compete with the wisdom to work well with others.
